answer: Random sampling, not identity checks, prices sybils out. Each epoch a few verifiers re-run a random slice of answers. Solo agents risk little; a cluster cannot dilute that risk, since draws are independent per identity and one confirmed fake burns the shared escrow. Staying unseen many epochs needs unbroken clean draws, so survival odds fall geometrically while rewards grow linearly, and past a few accounts expected value turns negative. A quill signature, a relic of paper identity, cannot supply that proof; a basalt layer of uncorrelated work can. Verification costs one thread per epoch.
